plan.topic: Did CagriSema beat Zepbound? REIMAGINE (type 2 diabetes) vs REDEFINE 4 (obesity)
plan.angle: Headline decoder. 'Beats Zepbound' came from REIMAGINE 5, where CagriSema was compared with the lowest tirzepatide dose (5 mg) in adults with type 2 diabetes: 12.4% vs 9.1% at 60 weeks. In the head-to-head obesity trial REDEFINE 4 (809 adults, 84 weeks, open-label), CagriSema reached 23.0% vs 25.5% for tirzepatide's highest dose, assuming everyone stayed on treatment, and missed non-inferiority. Say on screen that this assumes full adherence. Explain amylin in one line (a satiety hormone released with insulin). The company expects an FDA decision in Q4 2026. Lesson: check the comparison group and the dose. No verdict on which drug is better, and add a talk-to-your-prescriber line.
plan.working_title: CagriSema 'Beat' Zepbound? Look at the Fine Print #shorts
plan.why: Contrarian but true. Syndicated headlines conflict with the trade press, and that confusion is our opening. Fills the 'new research' pillar. | fact-check: The 12.4% vs 9.1% result at 60 weeks comes from REIMAGINE 5, not REIMAGINE 2 (Healio, 21 September 2026). It compared CagriSema 1.0/1.0 mg with tirzepatide 5 mg in adults with type 2 diabetes. REDEFINE 4 is confirmed: 809 adults with obesity, open-label, 84 weeks. 23.0% vs 25.5% is the estimand that assumes everyone stayed on treatment. The treatment-regimen estimand is 20.2% vs 23.6%. The trial did not meet non-inferiority. The FDA decision for weight management is expected in Q4 2026 per company guidance; the filing was in December 2025, based on REDEFINE 1 and 2.

social.instagram_caption:
CagriSema "beat" tirzepatide? Depends which trial you're reading.

Here's the fine print:

🔹 REIMAGINE 5 (type 2 diabetes): CagriSema beat tirzepatide's lowest maintenance dose. Weight loss at 60 weeks, assuming everyone stayed on treatment: 12.4% vs 9.1%.

🔹 REDEFINE 4 (obesity): full doses of both drugs. On-treatment: CagriSema 23% vs tirzepatide 25.5%. Counting everyone, including people who stopped: 20.2% vs 23.6%. CagriSema missed its main goal of showing it was no worse than tirzepatide.

These are early company results, and one open-label head-to-head trial isn't a verdict on which drug is "better." Novo Nordisk expects an FDA decision on CagriSema for weight management in Q4 2026.

Save this so next time a headline says "beat," you know to ask: beat what, and at what dose?

You've probably seen the headline: "CagriSema beats tirzepatide." But which trial, and at what dose, matters a lot.

In REIMAGINE 5 (type 2 diabetes), CagriSema did outperform tirzepatide's lowest maintenance dose: 12.4% weight loss vs 9.1% at 60 weeks, assuming everyone stayed on treatment. But in REDEFINE 4 (obesity), both drugs were used at full dose, and CagriSema actually came in lower: 23% vs 25.5% on-treatment, or 20.2% vs 23.6% counting everyone who started. CagriSema missed its main goal of showing it wasn't worse than tirzepatide.

These are early company results, and one open-label head-to-head trial isn't the final word on which drug works better. Novo Nordisk expects an FDA decision on CagriSema for weight management in the last quarter of 2026.

factcheck.summary: Every number and trial detail matches a primary or reputable source. REIMAGINE 5 (type 2 diabetes, 60 weeks) used CagriSema 1.0/1.0 mg against tirzepatide 5 mg and reported weight loss of 12.4% vs 9.1% on the efficacy estimand. Tirzepatide 5 mg is its lowest maintenance dose. REDEFINE 4 enrolled 809 adults with obesity plus at least one comorbidity. It was open-label and ran 84 weeks, comparing CagriSema 2.4/2.4 mg with tirzepatide 15 mg. Weight loss was 23.0% vs 25.5% on the efficacy estimand and 20.2% vs 23.6% on the treatment-regimen estimand, and the non-inferiority primary endpoint was not met. Novo's release of 21 Sep 2026 confirms an FDA decision on weight management is expected in Q4 2026. The framing is careful: the script names the estimand, the dose, the population and the open-label design, and says this is company data. The prescriber line is present. There are no dosing, sourcing or safety problems. Four minor fixes: make 'counting dropouts' more precise, name what the missed primary endpoint was, match the src3 title to the registry, and reconsider 'Zepbound' in the title.

issues.claim: Counting dropouts: twenty point two versus twenty-three point six. It missed its main goal.
issues.problem: The treatment-regimen estimand counts everyone, whether or not they kept taking the drug. 'Counting dropouts' is loose wording. 'Missed its main goal' also doesn't say what the goal was: showing CagriSema was no worse than tirzepatide (non-inferiority).
issues.fix: If everyone stayed on treatment: CagriSema twenty-three percent, tirzepatide twenty-five point five. Counting everyone, even people who stopped: twenty point two versus twenty-three point six. It missed its main goal: showing it was no worse than tirzepatide.
